```{r}
# Load required packages
library(tidyverse)  # For data wrangling (dplyr) and visualization (ggplot2)
library(lubridate)  # For handling start and end timestamps
library(gtsummary)  # For publication-ready demographic tables
library(psych)      # For Cronbach's alpha reliability analysis
library(dplyr)
# Set a clean theme for future plots
theme_set(theme_minimal())
```

```{r}

df_raw <- read_delim("metadata-demo.csv", delim = ";", col_names = TRUE)
colnames(df_raw)

```

```{r}
df_clean <- df_raw %>%
  mutate(
    # --- A. CHRONOMETRIC ANALYSIS ---
    start_time = ymd_hms(start),
    end_time = ymd_hms(end),
    completion_time_secs = as.numeric(difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "secs")),
    
    # Flag Speed-Responders (Threshold: under 90 seconds = 1, else 0)
    Time_Fail = if_else(completion_time_secs < 90, 1, 0),
    
    # --- B. GRADE THE IMCs (Instructional Manipulation Checks) ---
    # Target 1: 'strongly_disagree' | Target 2: 'option_c__insufficient_social_support'
    IMC_1_Fail = if_else(IMC_1 == "strongly_disagree", 0, 1, missing = 1),
    IMC_2_Fail = if_else(IMC_2 == "option_c__insufficient_social_support", 0, 1, missing = 1),
    
    # --- C. GRADE THE FACTUAL COMPREHENSION ---
    Fact_1_Fail = if_else(fact_1 == "serotonin", 0, 1, missing = 1),
    Fact_2_Fail = if_else(fact_2 == "catastrophizing", 0, 1, missing = 1),
    Fact_3_Fail = if_else(fact_3 == "deep_sleep__n3_stage___slow_wave_sleep", 0, 1, missing = 1),
    
    # --- D. CHECK INTERNAL CONSISTENCY (The straight-lining penalty) ---
    # pss_02a and pss_02b ask opposite concepts. If they answer the exact same number, flag it.
    Consist_Fail = if_else(pss_02a == pss_02b, 1, 0, missing = 0),
    
    # --- E. CALCULATE THE IER SPECTRUM SCORE (0 - 100) ---
    # Weights: IMC=20, Fact=10, Consist=15, Time=15
    IER_Score = (20 * (IMC_1_Fail + IMC_2_Fail)) + 
                (10 * (Fact_1_Fail + Fact_2_Fail + Fact_3_Fail)) + 
                (15 * Consist_Fail) + 
                (15 * Time_Fail),
    
    # --- F. CATEGORIZE BEHAVIORAL PHENOTYPES ---
    IER_Tier = case_when(
      IER_Score <= 15 ~ "Tier 0: Engaged",
      IER_Score <= 40 ~ "Tier 1: Skimmer",
      IER_Score <= 70 ~ "Tier 2: Satisficer",
      IER_Score > 70  ~ "Tier 3: Speed-Runner"
    ),
    # Convert Tier to a factor for proper ordering in tables/graphs
    IER_Tier = factor(IER_Tier, levels = c("Tier 0: Engaged", "Tier 1: Skimmer", "Tier 2: Satisficer", "Tier 3: Speed-Runner"))
  )
```

```{r}

df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Convert the raw text timestamps into actual datetime objects
    start_time = ymd_hms(start),
    end_time = ymd_hms(end),
    
    # 2. Calculate the difference in seconds (great for granular analysis)
    completion_time_secs = as.numeric(difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "secs")),
    
    # 3. Calculate the difference in minutes (as per your methodology)
    completion_time_mins = as.numeric(difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "mins"))
  )


summary(df_clean$completion_time_secs)
```

```{r}
# Ensure the package is loaded
library(gtsummary)

# Generate the cross-tabulation table
summary1 <- df_clean %>%
  # Select the demographic variables and our new IER_Tier
  select(MBBS_Year, Gender, Residential_status, previous_surveys, IER_Tier) %>%
  
  # Build the summary table, stratified by the IER Tier
  tbl_summary(
    by = IER_Tier,
    missing = "no", # Keeps the table clean by hiding 'unknown' missing data rows
    label = list(
      MBBS_Year ~ "Academic Year",
      Gender ~ "Sex",
      Residential_status ~ "Residential Status",
      previous_surveys ~ "Prior Survey Experience"
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # Automatically runs Chi-Squared tests across the tiers!
  add_p() %>%
  
  # Adds a bold, professional header
  modify_header(label = "**Demographic Characteristic**") %>%
  bold_labels()
```

```{r}
# Calculate overall prevalence of the IER Spectrum Tiers
ier_prevalence <- df_clean %>%
  count(IER_Tier, name = "Count") %>%
  mutate(
    Prevalence_Percentage = round((Count / sum(Count)) * 100, 1)
  )

# Print the table to the document
ier_prevalence
```

```{r}
# Note: Anyone not in "Tier 0: Engaged" constitutes your total IER prevalence.*

### 2. Prevalence of Specific Quality Flags

# Generate a prevalence table for the individual methodological flags
df_clean %>%
  # Select the specific binary failure flags we created in the mutate step
  select(Time_Fail, IMC_1_Fail, IMC_2_Fail, Consist_Fail) %>%
  
  # Build the summary table
  tbl_summary(
    statistic = all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)",
    missing = "no",
    label = list(
      Time_Fail ~ "Speed-Responder (< 90 seconds)",
      IMC_1_Fail ~ "Failed IMC 1 ('Strongly Disagree')",
      IMC_2_Fail ~ "Failed IMC 2 ('Option C')",
      Consist_Fail ~ "Failed Consistency Check (Straight-lining)"
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # Format the header for publication
  modify_header(label = "**Methodological Quality Indicator**") %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  modify_caption("**Table: Prevalence of Specific Survey Integrity Failures**")
```

```{r}
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Reverse score the positive PSS items (assuming a 0-3 scale, so 3 - x)
    pss_04_R = 3 - pss_04,
    pss_05_R = 3 - pss_05,
    pss_07_R = 3 - pss_07,
    pss_08_R = 3 - pss_08,
    
    # Calculate the Total PSS Score (just for completion's sake)
    Total_PSS = pss_01 + pss_02a + pss_03 + pss_04_R + pss_05_R + 
                pss_06 + pss_07_R + pss_08_R + pss_09 + pss_10,
    
    # 2. Calculate the Continuous Factual Error Count for the Inferential Tests
    Factual_Error_Count = Fact_1_Fail + Fact_2_Fail + Fact_3_Fail
  )
```

```{r}
library(psych)

# 1. Isolate the final 10 PSS items WITH the new reverse-scored columns
pss_items_correct <- df_clean %>%
  select(pss_01, pss_02a, pss_03, pss_04_R, pss_05_R, 
         pss_06, pss_07_R, pss_08_R, pss_09, pss_10)

# 2. Run the true Cronbach's alpha
true_alpha_results <- psych::alpha(pss_items_correct)

# 3. Print the summary
summary(true_alpha_results)
```

```{r}
# 1. Isolate only the careful responders
clean_pss_items <- df_clean %>%
  # Filter to keep ONLY Tiers 0 and 1
  filter(IER_Tier %in% c("Tier 0: Engaged", "Tier 1: Skimmer")) %>%
  
  # Select the 10 correct variables
  select(pss_01, pss_02a, pss_03, pss_04_R, pss_05_R, 
         pss_06, pss_07_R, pss_08_R, pss_09, pss_10)

# 2. Calculate the "Rescued" Alpha 
# (Keep this commented out until you have > 2 engaged students)
clean_alpha <- psych::alpha(clean_pss_items)
summary(clean_alpha)
```

```{r}
# First, let's create a single "Failed ANY IMC" flag for easier testing
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(Any_IMC_Fail = if_else(IMC_1_Fail == 1 | IMC_2_Fail == 1, 1, 0))

# 1. Does Academic Year predict failing an IMC?
cat("--- Association: MBBS Year vs. Failing an IMC ---\n")
chisq.test(df_clean$MBBS_Year, df_clean$Any_IMC_Fail)
# If sample is small, use Fisher's Exact Test instead:
# fisher.test(df_clean$MBBS_Year, df_clean$Any_IMC_Fail, simulate.p.value = TRUE)

# 2. Does Gender predict Speed-Responding?
cat("\n--- Association: Gender vs. Speed-Responding ---\n")
# Using Time_Fail which we defined as under 90 seconds
chisq.test(df_clean$Gender, df_clean$Time_Fail)
```

```{r}
# 1. Create the binary clinical status grouping
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  mutate(
    Clinical_Status = case_when(
      MBBS_Year %in% c("1st_year", "2nd_year") ~ "Pre-clinical",
      MBBS_Year %in% c("3rd_year", "final_year", "internship") ~ "Clinical",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    # Convert to factor for the t-test
    Clinical_Status = factor(Clinical_Status, levels = c("Pre-clinical", "Clinical"))
  )

# 2. Run the independent t-test
cat("--- Independent t-test: Factual Errors by Clinical Status ---\n")
t_test_results <- t.test(Factual_Error_Count ~ Clinical_Status, data = df_clean)
print(t_test_results)
```

```{r}
### 3. Time-on-Task Correlation (Spearman's $\rho$)
# This is the ultimate test of the Speed-Runner phenomenon. You are testing the hypothesis: *As completion time decreases, the number of factual errors increases.* Because completion times are highly skewed, we use the non-parametric Spearman method.

cat("--- Spearman Correlation: Completion Time vs Factual Errors ---\n")

# Run the correlation using the raw seconds column and the factual error count (0 to 3)
spearman_results <- cor.test(
  x = df_clean$completion_time_secs, 
  y = df_clean$Factual_Error_Count, 
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE # Prevents warnings about ties in the error count data
)

print(spearman_results)
```

```{r}
# Create a Scatterplot of Time vs. Errors with a Trend Line
ggplot(df_clean, aes(x = completion_time_secs, y = Factual_Error_Count)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0.1, alpha = 0.6, color = "darkblue") + # jitter prevents overlapping dots
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "The Speed-Running Effect",
    subtitle = "Inverse relationship between completion time and data accuracy",
    x = "Total Completion Time (Seconds)",
    y = "Number of Factual Errors (0-3)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
